transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start time: 16:30 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (HarborTrust Head of Security), Marc Dupree (HarborTrust Infra), Evan Li (HarborTrust Legal)

Summary (auto): Quick pass through HarborTrust security questionnaire with focus on KMS, RBAC, and data residency. Next steps: share SOC2, produce KMS guide, schedule follow-up deep dive.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today. Quick roll call, then we will jump into the HarborTrust security questionnaire.
[00:18] Asha: Hi, yes this is Asha, I'm head of security. Marc here too and Evan on legal, thanks.
[00:25] Marc: Hey.
[00:27] Evan: Hi all.
[00:29] Liam: Liam from Redwood, SE on the call. I'll cover the KMS and log ingestion bits.
[00:34] Sofia: Great. Our agenda was to walk the parts of the form you flagged as high priority — encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and residency. We can take questions as we go.
[00:46] Asha: Perfect. On encryption, our main ask is that keys are customer-managed through our KMS and we have control over key rotation. We also want to understand how logs are encrypted at rest.
[01:02] Liam: Absolutely. So quick overview: Redwood supports two KMS models. One is Redwood-managed keys where we store the DEK and wrap with our KMS; the other is customer-managed where you bring a CMK in your cloud KMS and we use external key wrap (EKW) with envelope encryption. For the questionnaire evidence we'll need to show the architecture diagram and the key lifecycle docs.
[01:28] Marc: When you say external key wrap, does that require network connectivity back to HarborTrust's KMS? We prefer not to open persistent channels from hosted instances to external key endpoints.
[01:40] Liam: Good question. The customer-managed mode requires outbound TLS calls to your KMS to perform unwrap operations during cold-start or when the DEK is rotated. We do cache the unwrapped DEK in-memory with strict TTL and HSM-backed protections. So it's not a constant chattering channel, but there are occasional calls.
[02:02] Asha: Hmm, okay. Is that compatible with an air-gapped or on-prem deployment? I know some of our regulated workloads are on-prem.
[02:10] Sofia: Redwood Private supports on-prem with a local KMS integration — for air-gapped scenarios we can ship an on-prem package that integrates with your internal HSM or Gateway KMS. That would be a separate arrangement and we have an enterprise checklist for that. I'll attach it.
[02:26] Evan: From legal side, we also need proof of key rotation policies and access logs for key usage. How granular are the logs?
[02:36] Liam: Key usage events are emitted to our audit stream with fields for key_id, operation, timestamp, requestor service id, and correlation id. We can provide sample JSON log lines as evidence. Note that if keys are customer-managed, key unwrap calls may appear as calls to your KMS in your own logs as well.
[02:56] Marc: You mentioned TTL for DEKs — how long do you hold them in memory? Our policy wants short TTLs, ideally under an hour.
[03:04] Liam: Default is 15 minutes for session DEKs, with rotation options down to 5 minutes. We can adjust for your profile.
[03:12] Asha: Good. Next on the list: RBAC and SSO. We need to map our internal roles to what Redwood exposes.
[03:20] Sofia: We have SSO with SAML and OIDC. Role mapping is configurable in the Redwood Console — you can map assertions to Redwood roles. Liam, do you want to show where that lives?
[03:29] Liam: Yes. The console supports SAML attribute mappings; we accept groups or role attributes and map them to Redwood roles like admin, ops, auditor, viewer. We also support SCIM for user provisioning so group membership sync is automated.
[03:43] Marc: Any logs of who assumed what role and when? We need auditor trails.
[03:49] Liam: Every auth event is captured in our audit logs with user id, role assigned, method (SSO/SCIM/Local), and timestamp. We also have session start/stop events so you can prove who did what during an audit period. We can provide a sample CSV export as evidence.
[04:06] Asha: Excellent. On the questionnaire there's a section about retention of audit logs and immutable storage. What's the retention configuration?
[04:15] Liam: You can configure retention per-customer in the console. Defaults are 90 days hot, archived up to seven years depending on plan. For regulatory needs we can push logs to your storage bucket with object-lock (WORM) settings. We recently added an S3-compatible archive connector for customers who require long-term immutable retention.
[04:37] Evan: If you push to our bucket, does Redwood still have access to those archives? We need to be sure only our auditors can access archived logs.
[04:45] Sofia: If you configure push-to-customer-bucket, access control is entirely in your policy — Redwood writes with a temporary role and then the objects are under your account. We still maintain an index for search if you permit it, but that can be disabled.
[04:58] Asha: Good to know. On data residency — we need all PII for EU customers to stay in eu-west-1. Is Redwood able to pin regions per-tenant?
[05:08] Liam: Yes, we offer per-tenant region pinning in Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private. For hosted customers we can set the default region and optionally replicate copies for DR in other regions, but primary processing and storage can be pinned to eu-west-1. Note: some managed services (like certain third-party monitoring) may still be US-based unless you choose Dedicated.
[05:30] Marc: That third-party monitoring callout worries us. Can we get a list of third-party subprocessors and where they host?
[05:36] Sofia: Absolutely, we have a subprocessors list and locations — we'll include that in the evidence bundle.
[05:41] Asha: On the SIG/CAIQ, there are a few items about penetration testing cadence and results. Do you do external pentests and can you provide redacted reports?
[05:50] Liam: Yes, annual third-party pentests. We can provide redacted executive summaries and remediation trackers. Full technical reports are available under NDA; we can set up an NDA request process.
[06:02] Evan: We'll likely request the redacted report first.
[06:05] Sofia: Noted. We'll add that to the action items.
[06:08] [08:34] Speaker 1: (unrelated background noise)
[06:12] Asha: Another question on evidence: for SIG item CC-07 around data destruction, what's your process when a customer requests deletion?
[06:20] Liam: We support immediate deprovisioning of tenant keys and controlled deletion of persisted data. The process is: request, scheduled wipe, verification scans, and a deletion certificate. For archival objects pushed to customer buckets, Redwood will remove pointers but actual object deletion is controlled by the customer account unless you request Redwood to perform deletion operations via cross-account roles.
[06:44] Marc: Is the deletion certificate cryptographically signed? Our compliance team prefers signed attestations.
[06:50] Liam: We can provide a signed attestation using Redwood's signing key — that's part of our enterprise package. We'll include an example.
[07:00] Asha: We also flagged questions on incident response and notification timelines for security incidents.
[07:06] Sofia: Our standard is notify customers within 72 hours for incidents that meet criteria, with a detailed post-mortem within 14 days. For Dedicated customers with SLA we can shorten that window.
[07:18] Evan: Any customers we've had incidents with that you can redact as references?
[07:23] Sofia: We have anonymized incident summaries we can share; again, we'll redact PII.
[07:27] Liam: One clarification on logging: we emit structured JSON logs with fields for trace ids. If you want us to ship logs to your SIEM, we support syslog, Kinesis, and direct S3 ingestion. There's a small delta in latency for near-real-time (under 30s) vs archive.
[07:47] Asha: For audit purposes we need immutable storage for 5 years and daily digests. Can Redwood generate daily signed digests of logs?
[07:55] Liam: Yes, we can produce daily digests signed with our signing key, or you can opt to have digests generated in your environment by pushing raw logs to your bucket and running your own digest pipeline.
[08:06] Marc: On RBAC mapping, we need an 'auditor' role that is read-only and cannot access data in the clear. Is that supported?
[08:14] Liam: Yes, the auditor role is read-only and is segmented from any key-unwrap capabilities; access to plaintext is gated by key permissions. So auditors can see metadata and logs but not plaintext token outputs unless explicitly permitted.
[08:28] Asha: Okay great. There are a few SIG items about boundary protection and network hardening. Can you share your network diagram and firewall rules?
[08:37] Sofia: We'll include a redacted network diagram and an overview of our boundary controls. For Hosted, the control plane sits in a separate tenant and operator access is RBACed and logged. For Dedicated/Private we can provide more detailed diagrams under NDA.
[08:52] Evan: One more legal item — we need to confirm your standard data processing addendum and whether it supports our controller/processor model.
[09:00] Sofia: Our DPA supports both controller/processor and processor/subprocessor relationships and is fairly standard; we'll send the template. If you need modifications, legal can loop.
[09:09] Asha: Thanks. For the evidence delivery, we prefer an encrypted zip pushed to our secure SFTP or to our customer bucket. We don't want links via email.
[09:20] Sofia: Understood — we can put the redacted evidence bundle in an encrypted tarball, upload to your S3 bucket (pre-signed URL with restricted IP) or SFTP. We'll follow HarborTrust's preference; note that SOC2 reports also require our signing attestations.
[09:38] Liam: I'm going to call out one technical nuance: when you opt for KMS customer-managed, some of the CAIQ questions about key custody change because your KMS will show certain operations in your logs. We'll annotate those CAIQ items to show which evidence should come from HarborTrust KMS logs vs Redwood logs.
[10:00] Marc: That helps. Can you also map the SIG/CC items to our questionnaire rows? We have an excel with row ids.
[10:09] Sofia: Yes, please send the spreadsheet. We'll do a mapping matrix and return it. Add that to action items.
[10:16] Asha: On the topic of multi-tenancy, we need assurance that tenant isolation is enforced, and that one tenant cannot access another's models or KV caches.
[10:26] Liam: Isolation is enforced at multiple layers: per-tenant encryption keys, per-tenant model instances, and runtime namespace isolation. KV cache entries are namespaced per-tenant and cryptographically scoped. We'll provide a short technical note and sample config showing namespacing.
[10:44] Asha: Good. Are there any known limitations or caveats we should be aware of for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[10:51] Sofia: Hosted is fastest to onboard but has more limited region isolation for some add-on services. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and full isolation including network controls, but procurement and lead time are longer. Private on-prem gives the most control but requires a longer integration window. We'll sketch the tradeoffs in the follow-up doc.
[11:12] Evan: For procurement, we'll likely start with Hosted with strict region pinning and then evaluate Dedicated based on performance tests.
[11:20] Sofia: Sounds like a solid plan. For follow-ups: we'll send the SOC2 package, subprocessors list, redacted pen test summary, network diagram, KMS guide, and the SIG-to-question mapping. We'll target the technical deep dive next Thursday.
[11:36] Asha: One quick question — can you provide an example of the audit log format? A few lines of sample JSON would help our compliance team.
[11:45] Liam: Yes, I'll attach a small sample JSON file with typical fields.
[11:49] Marc: Also Terraform snippet for the KMS role and policies would be helpful so our infra team can pre-approve before the deep dive.
[11:58] Liam: I'll include that.
[12:00] Sofia: Okay, thanks everyone. Any final questions?
[12:04] Evan: Not from legal, thanks.
[12:06] Asha: No, that covers it.
[12:08] Sofia: Great — I'll follow up with the bundle and calendar invite for the follow-up deep dive. Thanks all.
[12:14] Liam: Thanks.
[12:16] Marc: Bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., "kay-em-ess" for KMS, "V-P-Cee" for VPC), speaker overlaps at 06:08 and slight background noise around 08:34.
